sentences.text: Dadagavialis is a member of the family Gavialidae, a group of long-snouted crocodilians.
This species is distinguished from all other gavialoids by having a prefrontal process that is wider than the prefrontal bone at the level of the anterior orbital margin.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a partial skull preserving a section of the snout, part of the cranial vault, and a partial neurocranium.
Dadagavialis was first described by scientists in 2018.

The genus name combines the Guna word "dada" for "ancient" with the Greek word "gavialis", while the species name "gunai" honors the Guna people, who are known as enthusiastic navigators of the Caribbean.
When described, Dadagavialis was proposed to belong to the subfamily Gryposuchinae, a subfamily of gavials that was primarily found in South America.

This extinct crocodilian lived during the Early Miocene in the region that is now Panama, specifically within the Cucaracha Formation between 18.5 and 16.3 million years ago during the Burdigalian stage.
During the Early Miocene, central Panama formed the southernmost part of the North American continent, bordering the Central American Seaway.
Some researchers argue that Dadagavialis should be classified directly within Gavialidae because Gryposuchinae is considered an evolutionary grade rather than a distinct clade.
